history.period: Legendary Mahabharata-era (Pandavas); actual construction date unverified
history.summary: TOWN/STATE CORRECTION: the documented Kali Mata temple matching this row is at Kalka, Panchkula district, HARYANA - not Solan, Himachal Pradesh (CSV town and state both wrong). It stands on NH-22 at Kalka, about 2 km from Parwanoo (Solan district, HP) near the HP-Haryana border. An ancient shrine to Goddess Kali; legend says it was built by the Pandavas during their exile (Agyatvas), and the city of Kalka takes its name from this temple. It draws heavy pilgrim crowds at Navratri. IDENTITY AMBIGUITY: 'Kali Mata Temple, Solan' is a generic name with other candidates - the Kali Ka Tibba shrine inside the Mohan Shakti Heritage Park and Shoolini Mata (a form of Kali) in Solan city; documented here is the best-known Kalka/Parwanoo shrine, flagged for confirmation.

name: Prachin Shree Kali Mata Temple, Kalka
town_description: Kalka is a town in Panchkula district, Haryana, at the foothills of the Shivaliks on NH-22, about 14 km from Chandigarh. It is the terminus of the broad-gauge rail line and the starting point of the Kalka-Shimla heritage narrow-gauge railway; the town is said to take its name from the Kali temple.

travel.railway: Kalka railway station, within the town (terminus of the Kalka-Shimla line)
travel.road: On NH-22 (Shimla Road), Kalka; ~2 km from Parwanoo across the HP-Haryana border

visitor_information.best_time: March-June and September-November; Navratri is the peak period
visitor_information.opening_hours: Official visiting hours not published - verify locally
